body:
Read together, the three texts disagree about remedies but reduce, on inspection, to two empirical questions the flat itself can answer. Is the recurring trouble underspecification (the account) or the negotiation structure itself (the rival)? And what is the avoider avoiding — the tone of the talks (the account), governance as such (the rival), or possibly the asker, which the objection's single-source caution cannot exclude? Since none of these can be settled from the material, the right continuation is not to pick a diagnosis but to pick an order: cheap, reversible moves, ranked by how little participation they need, each carrying an observation that discriminates among the surviving hypotheses. That converts the objection's sharpest point — 'not a test, a bet' — into a design rule rather than a verdict.

What I keep from the account is what the objection also keeps: expiry-and-review, and the explicit surfacing of possible imbalance, both sound independently of the ambiguity hypothesis. What I take from the objection and act on: anything written down is co-authored at the moment of agreement, or the confirmation runs the other way, from the non-drafting party — because the record is contested ground and a one-party record is one person's interpretation with a date on it. I adopt the objection's discriminating observation (do disputes recur specifically over recorded, time-limited items?) and add one for its suppression worry: resolved conflict tends to end, suppressed conflict tends to migrate into new topics, tone, lateness, character. Migration is imperfect as a proxy but it is the observable difference between acquiescence and resolution. And I accept the non-attendance point as grounds for reordering: a plan whose first step is a meeting is thin exactly where this flat is thickest. From the rival I take the pose-shift — what can the asker do now, possibly alone — while declining its negotiation-economy thesis as a default; the rival itself names the local disconfirmation (a simple note actually ending the disputes), so it stays a live hypothesis the sequence will test. The objection's internal-tension point resolves by scope: 'agree less' governs how many arrangements exist, 'write it down' governs the few that remain; they conflict only if applied globally.

One correction the whole exchange missed: in three texts nobody assigns the third flatmate any role. Everything known comes from one narrator, and the cheapest available repair is to compare perceptions with flatmate three before any avoider-directed move — are the disputes about meaning, load, tone? This is error-correction, not coalition-building; if it cannot be had without becoming recruitment against the avoider, it should be skipped, since ganging-up would confirm every bad reading of the talks. And a methodological rule the exchange also missed: one lever at a time, with pauses. All three texts propose bundles, but bundling destroys the signal — if you co-author notes, hire a cleaner, and re-partition the same fortnight and things improve, you learn nothing about which hypothesis survived.

The sequence I end up with, and why this order. First, self-binding partition: the asker claims a visible domain outright — the kitchen, say, permanently, to a stated standard, complaints invited — and carries it without demanding reciprocity for a while. An announcement can bind the announcer but creates no obligations for others, so it is fully within the asker's control and robust even to the uncomfortable hypothesis that the asker is part of the problem. Silence conscripts no one: no other domains are assigned, and anything unclaimed stays unowned rather than defaulting to the least avoidant flatmate — that default is the trap the objection located in 'stop treating silence as agreement.' The probe: if whose-turn disputes over the owned domain die, ownership kills that class of fight, favouring the rival's structure reading over pure ambiguity. Second, money conversion: a cleaner fortnightly, split three ways, pending budget slack, which none of us can verify. It needs one agreement about money rather than character, and it is diagnostic: if removing most of the labour removes most of the conflict, the chores were the cause; if fighting survives the removal, the chores were the venue. Third, week-sized deals for the remnant — whatever neither partition nor money covers is allocated in seven-day units, agreed in the moment, too small to litigate; at these stakes a confirmation line is proportionate, but per the revision it comes from, or is co-written with, the non-drafting party. Fourth, for the avoider, exits before meetings. I adopt the rival's replacement of the account's process one-to-one on three grounds: an exit is cheaper to accept than a meeting is to attend; choice behaviour is better evidence than self-report about what the talks feel like; and the move is remedy and test in one. The objection's caveat rides along: the response is evidence, not verdict. An exit taken with relief says governance was the object; refusal of both exits and engagement is consistent with withdrawal from the friendship, with grievance at the asker, and with circumstances nothing here can see — so it must not be chalked up as diagnosis of the avoider, only as localising the problem somewhere under the chores. What remains then is the conversation the rival rightly says cannot be pre-scripted, approached in the account's tone: acknowledgment first, on their terms, no chore content on the table. Fifth, the review survives but moves house: no longer the engine of a system (there may be no system), it is the explicit check on the fairness fork — do the now-public domains and the money split look balanced? Partition has been doing quiet work here all along, because fixed domains make loads comparable in a way rotating tacit splits never could; a grievance that ran in either direction becomes statable and checkable instead of deniable.

What I set aside: records as neutral infrastructure (rejected on the objection's grounds; among contesting intimates a record is a move, so records are sized to stakes); the process one-to-one as the opener (retained only as the fallback above); and costless 'silence is not agreement' — the admitted price of dropping it is that non-decision privileges whoever is content with the status quo, and my only counter is that the asker's visible ownership shifts what the status quo is, which may not compensate in every flat.

Two problems survive everything here. The unowned commons: if the avoider claims no domain, takes no exit, and money is short, something remains that someone must absorb, price, or deliberately let slide — and letting it slide re-creates the tacit expectations that generate disputes, by the account's own mechanism, so at minimum the choice must be made consciously by the person who will bear it. And the boundary case: enough non-engagement converts a chore problem into a question about the living arrangement itself, which none of the three texts addresses; I leave it open rather than pretend to close it.

Finally, I take up the rival's closing constraint without revision: the failure mode is three friends becoming litigants, and several of these remedies — records, pricing, exits — push the flat toward counterparty-ness even when they work. So the friendship is maintained on purpose, in time that is not flat administration, as a standing condition of the sequence. Conveniently, the early warning of that failure — conflict migrating from chores into character — is the same observation I named as the suppression probe: one watching brief guards the friendship and the diagnosis at once.
commitments: Taking this up commits one to the following. Two inherited conjectures are carried as rivals, neither established: the ambiguity reading from p.response.0 and the negotiation-economy reading from p.response.2, plus the still-open fairness fork; adopting the sequence means adopting it as a probe sequence, and anyone who wants certainty before acting should not take it up, since no step is evidence-proof. Dependences flagged: the partition move and the exit offer depend on the asker's ability to carry a self-announced share reliably, possibly without reciprocity; the money move depends on budget slack that cannot be verified from the material; the entire ordering rests on one sentence of the original task ('has started avoiding the conversations') being a fair description. Proposed discriminating observations I commit to refining or dropping under challenge: recurrence-over-recorded-items (inherited from the objection); conflict migration as the suppression-versus-resolution proxy (mine, admittedly noisy — suppression can also present as simple withdrawal — so anyone adopting it takes on that caveat); exit-taken-with-relief as the avoider diagnostic (adopted with the objection's warning that refusal is multiply interpretable and must not be recorded as a character verdict). Revisions whose grounds I inherit and would have to defend: joint authorship of anything written and the scaling of record-keeping to stakes, both resting on the contested-record argument; reordering moves by buy-in required, resting on the objection's non-attendance point and the rival's ordering principle. A methodological commitment beyond the sources: one lever at a time with observation gaps — bundle everything and the diagnostics are lost, at which point the sequence is exactly the unargued bet the objection accused the account of offering. The third-flatmate consultation is proposed as error-correction only; taking it up includes the constraint that it be dropped if it cannot be structured so as to be unexperienceable as recruitment. Retained from the account, on the objection's grounds: expiry-and-review and explicit surfacing of imbalance. Rejected in unmodified form, with the obligation to argue against their revival: unilateral confirmation messages, a process-first one-to-one as opener, and costless silence-is-not-agreement; the admitted weakness of the replacement is that visible ownership may not fully compensate for what non-decision hands the status-quo-contented. Two unresolved problems are named and not solved: the unowned commons if exits and money both fail, and the boundary where the chore problem becomes the viability of the arrangement — no conversation for that case is scripted here. The friendship-maintenance condition constrains all of the above: remedies that work as administration while converting friends into counterparties count as failures, and the migration probe doubles as its early warning. Nothing here commits anyone to escalation, to hiring help regardless of cost, or to ending the arrangement; and if my reading of the three inputs is wrong, the pieces to salvage first are the buy-in ordering and the rule that every remedy arrive carrying its discriminating observation.
